paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Proverbs 20 is a whole bakery shelf of wisdom, and it all points at one thing. Live honest, live awake, and let the LORD run the scoreboard. Solomon says differing weights and unequal measures are "detestable to the LORD" (Proverbs 20:10), and he says food gained by fraud ends with a mouth "full of gravel" (Proverbs 20:17). The shortcut tastes sweet for one bite, and then you're chewing gravel.

Now here's the part that gets me. Solomon asks, "Who can say, 'I have kept my heart pure; I am cleansed from my sin'?" (Proverbs 20:9). The answer is nobody, and that's a humbling thing to hear, so I'll say it plain: none of us gets to stand over the wisdom pile like a judge. Even our steps are from the LORD (Proverbs 20:24), so we walk humble, and we ask for help instead of faking it.

That leads to the verse the whole chapter leans on: "Do not say, 'I will avenge this evil!' Wait on the LORD, and He will save you." (Proverbs 20:22). Somebody wrongs you, and everything in you wants to get even RIGHT NOW. But waiting isn't weakness, friend. It's trusting that the One who sees everything is already on the job. So hand Him the hurt, keep your own scales honest, and go bake something good.
